sourceFeature.text: Offline ASR transcription and local model routing
sourceFeature.acceptanceText: CPU and GPU speech observations produce source-clock word spans, language, effective model, scores and honest uncertainty; no synthetic transcript qualifies.

capabilities.label: Transcribe audio file
capabilities.outcome: File transcription is represented by a tracking reference and, if produced, an unverified transcript draft linked to the source version/timebase with provided language or recognition evidence. When explicitly requested and admitted, transcription may use a versioned custom glossary for recognition or correction and may return uncertain source-anchored filler-word or retake candidates. Glossary guidance is distinct from punctuation/capitalization formatting; filler/retake candidates are distinct from silence observations and do not alter the source.
explicitUnsupportedCases: No implicit supported-language list, default locale, confidence threshold, speaker identification, diarization guarantee, file duration/size, sample-rate, or provider is defined here.
No claim that returned transcript text is human-verified, an accessible caption, or a registered caption version.

conditionalSemantics.meaning: Identify the exact admitted glossary version used; if it is unsupported or unavailable, report UNAVAILABLE or reject without silently omitting glossary guidance.
Return only uncertain source-version/time-anchored candidates, distinct from silence observations and without source deletion or edit.

constraints: Glossary use does not verify transcript correctness.
An unavailable or unsupported glossary is not silently treated as applied.

fields.timeRange: Source-time range associated with each uncertain candidate.

constraints: Silence alone is not a filler/retake classification.
Candidate observations never delete, trim, or cut source content.

capabilityAcceptanceCases.given: Audio source, current rights/consent, requested language, profile, and required bounds are admitted.
capabilityAcceptanceCases.then: The response returns one durable job identity and the requested operation/profile version without claiming a transcript is complete or verified.

capabilityAcceptanceCases.given: The job produces partial or uncertain recognition.
capabilityAcceptanceCases.then: The result preserves source version/timebase, labels recognized text as unverified, scopes uncertainty to supplied evidence, and exposes a review path.

capabilityAcceptanceCases.given: Language, format, consent, or qualification is unknown or denied.
capabilityAcceptanceCases.then: The operation blocks or returns only a permitted partial result with explicit limitation; no language or speaker identity is invented.

requirements.statement: Every operation in media.speech.transcription retains the intended semantic outcome in the full product definition and is invocable only through an explicit, authorized, compatible binding whose current implementation, license admission, qualification, and runtime availability are separately established.
requirements.expectedBehavior: The system performs only the requested File and streaming STT; language detection; voice-activity detection; speaker diarization, segmentation and separation; authorized speaker identification; word and phoneme timestamps; forced alignment; punctuation/capitalization; alternatives and confidence; speech translation; subtitle generation operation using typed inputs and outputs; reports actual effective parameters and provenance; preserves source versions; and does not substitute an unsupported engine, model, format, language, or delivery profile silently.
failureDegradationRecovery: Return typed validation, authority, rights/license, unsupported-capability, capacity, timeout, cancellation, provider-ambiguity, and internal-failure outcomes as applicable.
Expose safe remediation, retry/cancel/reconcile eligibility, and finality; do not silently downgrade preservation, quality, spatial/scientific fidelity, or delivery constraints.
Preserve accepted source and completed outputs; require policy-permitted explicit fallback or stop for review.

citedParentCases.given: A declared leaf, authorized input, and a binding that satisfies the requested profile and policy.
citedParentCases.when: The caller requests the operation.
citedParentCases.then: The typed result, effective parameters, provenance, terminal/finality state, and measured dimensions are returned; only the declared effect occurs.

citedParentCases.given: The requested language, format, right, profile, license, capability, or qualification is absent or unknown.
citedParentCases.when: Admission is evaluated.
citedParentCases.then: The operation is blocked or returns an explicit qualified fallback only when policy permits; unknown is never reported as available.

citedParentCases.given: A user explicitly initiates dictation and selects a target that is authorized by the operating system.
citedParentCases.when: the product inserts the resulting dictated text into that selected target.
citedParentCases.then: limit capture and insertion to the user-initiated session and selected OS-authorized target; report unavailable when permission or the required adapter is missing.
citedParentCases.rejection: reject background or global capture/insertion, choosing an unselected target, or bypassing denied or unavailable permission.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized source version and an admitted, versioned custom glossary are supplied for transcription.
citedParentCases.when: Glossary-guided recognition or correction is requested.
citedParentCases.then: Return any produced transcript as an unverified, source-version/timebase-linked draft and identify the glossary version used; keep this operation distinct from punctuation and capitalization.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject silently applying an ambiguous, unsupported, or unavailable glossary entry, or claiming that glossary guidance verifies transcript correctness.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized source version is admitted for speech transcription and filler/retake analysis.
citedParentCases.when: The actor requests ASR-assisted filler-word or retake detection.
citedParentCases.then: Return only uncertain candidate observations anchored to the exact source version and time range, distinct from silence observations.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject classifying silence alone as a filler or retake, or automatically deleting, trimming, or cutting source content from a candidate observation.

citedParentCases.given: A user requests translation of a source speech or transcript version to a declared target locale and supplies any translation-memory or brand-glossary references and approved term entries available for that request.
citedParentCases.when: The translation operation is evaluated and, if admitted, prepares a translated draft.
citedParentCases.then: Apply only admitted, versioned, approved, unambiguous, applicable source/target term pairs or do-not-translate entries; preserve the memory and glossary versions and identify which protected terms were retained. Present translated content as a draft, not as approved or verified text. For an otherwise admitted translation request with a missing or unavailable memory or glossary, explicitly report that it was not applied; do not silently substitute another entry, glossary, or translation behavior. If a supplied memory or glossary is denied, stale, ambiguous, conflicting, or unknown, report that state; if source authorization or rights are denied or unknown, block the operation under the family admission behavior in MEDIA-REQ-CAP-SPEECH-TRANSCRIPTION-AC-02 with no fallback. For any dubbed result, preserve every supplied per-segment speaker, locale, source-timing, and translation-provenance field. If a field is not supplied or cannot be established, identify it as absent or unknown rather than silently omitting or fabricating it; mark a field not applicable only with an explicit reason. This case does not establish audio/video export synchronization, which remains a separate requirement.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject changing a term marked do-not-translate, silently omitting an unresolved protected term, applying an unversioned, unapproved, or inapplicable entry, resolving conflicting entries by silent preference, or describing a translated draft as owner-approved or verified.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized microphone recording session and an admitted transcription request refer to the same exact captured source version.
citedParentCases.when: The product prepares a transcript draft or paired archive candidate.
citedParentCases.then: Link the transcript to the source version, capture session, and timebase while retaining the recording as an independently identifiable immutable artifact.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject implying archive registration, changing either artifact without separate authorization, or claiming a resolved pair when source identity or alignment is unknown.

priorProposalR1.proposalRationale: The search leaf supports authorized transcript/rights/timeline/person/speaker-facet searches within an exact immutable source/project version and time scope; it requires affirmative rights evidence for the declared use and excludes external catalog search.

upstreamCapabilityEvidence.outcome: Return a bounded page of authorized governed records within the supplied exact immutable source-media or project version and any declared source-time range. citedParentCases.rejection: Reject presenting candidates as complete when matching or continuation is unknown, or returning transcript content outside the admitted rights-and-retention scope.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized Studio creator searches the governed Media asset store for candidates for an explicitly declared intended-use scope.
citedParentCases.when: The product evaluates each immutable asset version for the requested license/use-scope filter.
citedParentCases.then: Return a candidate as eligible only when current authoritative per-version rights and license evidence explicitly permits the declared scope; preserve the exact asset version and evidence identity. citedParentCases.rejection: Reject inferring permission from searchable metadata, treating this filter as legal clearance, silently substituting a different asset or license, or claiming external-catalog search, ranking, or complete results.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized editor searches an admitted project for timeline, person, scene, or speaker facets with an explicit time range and exact project or source-version scope.
citedParentCases.when: The product evaluates the requested facet filters against indexed observations.
citedParentCases.then: Return bounded matches with exact immutable source-version references, matching time ranges, and observed or inferred provenance; report unknown or unindexed fields and partial matching separately from a known empty result.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject presenting an unindexed or uncertain facet as absent, claiming complete matches while continuation or indexing is unknown, or widening the search beyond authorized rights and retention scope.

citedParentCases.then: Return bounded candidate matches with exact source-version provenance, relevant time ranges where available, and match uncertainty; distinguish unavailable or unindexed evidence and unknown matching from a known empty result.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject representing similarity as a verified fact, dropping source-version provenance, claiming completeness when indexing or continuation is unknown, or exposing content outside admitted rights and retention scope.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized editor imports a sidecar or embedded caption track for an exact immutable media version and the format and rights are admitted.
citedParentCases.when: The product parses and validates the caption source and its timebase mapping.
citedParentCases.then: Return a reviewable caption-import result preserving source-file provenance, source version, language and format when known, caption timing, and any conversion or alignment uncertainty; do not alter the source media.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject silently shifting or dropping caption timing, claiming unknown language or alignment as verified, or registering or replacing a canonical artifact without the separately authorized action.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized editor requests a clip derived from an exact immutable source version with an explicit source-time range, output profile, purpose, and applicable rights.
citedParentCases.when: The product validates the range against the source timebase and prepares the derivation.
citedParentCases.then: Bind the candidate derivation to the exact source version and requested start and end times, disclose boundary quantization or uncertainty, and return job or candidate state without changing the source.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject substituting another source version, silently rounding or extending the requested range, implying a completed or registered artifact before that state is confirmed, or bypassing rights and profile admission.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized user searches the governed Media asset store by declared metadata and an intended-use rights scope.
citedParentCases.when: The product evaluates exact asset versions against available metadata and authoritative per-version rights evidence.
citedParentCases.then: Return bounded candidates with exact version and rights-evidence references; distinguish unknown or incomplete indexing from a known empty result. External catalogs are available only when a specific catalog and use are separately admitted.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject inferring permission from searchable metadata, calling search legal clearance, or claiming external-catalog, complete, or ranked results when those scopes are not admitted.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized editor supplies a source timecode with its exact source version, declared frame rate or timebase, and drop-frame or non-drop-frame mode.

citedParentCases.rejection: Reject ambiguous or invalid labels, mismatched rates, unknown mappings, silent drop-frame/non-drop-frame reinterpretation, or rounding across frame boundaries.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized presenter script and an explicit scene/narration cue map are supplied for a recording session.
citedParentCases.when: The presenter uses the recording teleprompter.
citedParentCases.then: Present the script prompt synchronized to the declared active cue and retain its script and cue provenance.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject inferring cue alignment when the map is absent, or treating prompt presentation as a committed recording or project edit.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized creator declares a recording-take intent such as ADR or room tone, identifies its session, source context, and intended placement, and starts a governed capture session.
citedParentCases.when: The product observes the recording session or its terminal capture state.
citedParentCases.then: Return a typed take-intent and capture-observation record with session, timing, and provenance, distinguishing captured, unavailable, interrupted, and finality-unknown outcomes; this observation alone does not commit a media artifact or project edit.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject describing an intent or partial observation as a completed take, silently attaching or registering captured media, or conflating captured ADR with generated narration or generated room tone.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized capture request includes a verified, source-time-bound click or typed-action observation and an eligible framing intent.
citedParentCases.when: The product proposes an action-linked zoom or focus change.
citedParentCases.then: Return a local framing candidate tied to the exact action evidence, source version, time interval, and uncertainty; the proposal does not change or render the source.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject describing inferred focus as verified, proposing action-linked framing without action evidence, or applying the proposal without separate confirmation.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized capture request declares privacy masking for keyboard or pointer overlays and the applicable policy marks an event sensitive or its classification unknown.
citedParentCases.when: The product captures or prepares the corresponding event observation.
citedParentCases.then: Omit or mask sensitive payload and retain only policy-permitted event and timing data; when the masking policy or detector state is unknown, block raw overlay capture or mask the full affected interval.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject retaining or displaying unmasked sensitive input by default, inferring that an event is non-sensitive from missing classification, or treating policy absence as consent.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized actor requests a consequential product action and identifies the authoritative system and readback channel for its claimed effect.
citedParentCases.when: Media observes an action acknowledgment and evaluates the effect readback.
citedParentCases.then: Report acknowledgment separately from authoritative readback, binding readback to its exact source, version, observation time, and state; absent, conflicting, stale, or unknown readback remains UNKNOWN or UNAVAILABLE.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject reporting the product effect as successful from a click, command, local acknowledgment, or Media execution record alone.

citedParentCases.given: A creator requests conversational text composition, rewriting, or a response to a user-provided utterance or context for a declared voice/personality profile.
citedParentCases.when: the system prepares proposed response text for speech synthesis.
citedParentCases.then: treat the response as system-authored content distinct from speaker-conditioned audio; preserve its declared request/context provenance and the identity boundary; distinguish supplied, quoted, and generated content; label factual claims as unverified unless supported by an explicitly linked source and its applicable review.
citedParentCases.rejection: reject implying that voice conditioning authored, verified, or authorized response text or its claims; reject presenting generated text as a user statement, verified fact, or approved communication.

citedParentCases.given: A creator requests singing-voice synthesis conditioned on an identifiable voice, source recording, or voice model.
citedParentCases.when: the product produces a permitted synthesis result.
citedParentCases.then: retain the declared voice, source, and model provenance with the resulting media.
citedParentCases.rejection: reject omitting the provenance needed to distinguish the source and model used for the derived voice result.

citedParentCases.given: A user explicitly starts a full-duplex voice conversation and authorizes a live speech-input session; the streaming transcription and streaming synthesis leaves are separately admitted for the requested scope.
citedParentCases.when: Media concurrently receives live speech input and prepares or returns a generated spoken response for the current conversational turn.
citedParentCases.then: provide a response attributable to the current user-initiated turn, distinguish observed or transcribed input from generated response text and synthesized audio, expose whether the turn is still streaming or complete, and preserve interruption and cancellation as explicit outcomes; do not modify a project or publish a response as a separate effect.
citedParentCases.rejection: reject hidden or background microphone capture, continuing capture after the user ends the session, representing partial or uncertain recognition as confirmed input, or reporting a complete response when the outcome is unknown or unavailable.

citedParentCases.given: A creator supplies an authorized narration or text source with ordered chapter and paragraph boundaries and requests an audiobook output in a declared M4B profile.
citedParentCases.when: Media prepares the requested speech artifact and audiobook package.
citedParentCases.then: Preserve the supplied chapter and paragraph order and boundaries in the audiobook candidate, bind the requested voice and source provenance to that candidate, and expose the requested M4B package and metadata only as candidate properties. If authorization, source/audio/voice/package rights or license, M4B format support, profile admission, or qualification is denied, absent, or unknown, apply MEDIA-REQ-CAP-SPEECH-SYNTHESIS-AC-02; never report the requested format as available on unknown evidence or imply completed delivery.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject flattening or reordering supplied boundaries, inventing chapter metadata, silently substituting a format or voice, or representing candidate metadata as proof of qualified format support, completed audio, or delivery.

citedParentCases.given: A creator supplies an authorized, rights-cleared source, ordered text segments, and an authorized, rights-cleared, admitted voice/personality profile with the exact shared context intended to govern their synthesis.
citedParentCases.when: Media prepares speech for those segments as one continuous work.
citedParentCases.then: Represent the declared segment order and shared context/profile as requested candidate properties; report continuity as established only for segments where the admitted operation establishes it, and expose other segments as denied, unsupported, or unknown. Apply MEDIA-REQ-CAP-SPEECH-SYNTHESIS-AC-02 if source, voice, profile, authorization, rights, or license admission is denied, absent, or unknown; a candidate property does not guarantee audible continuity.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject claiming cross-segment continuity from unrelated or missing context, silently changing the declared profile, or treating an unavailable or unknown continuity result as established or guaranteeing audible identity/continuity.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized creator supplies an ordered story or speech plan with explicit segment boundaries and an authorized speaker assignment for each segment.
citedParentCases.when: The product prepares or generates speech for the ordered segments.
citedParentCases.then: Preserve segment order and boundaries, bind each segment to its exact authorized speaker and applicable rights evidence, and return per-segment voice, source, and generated-audio provenance with any unavailable assignment marked explicitly.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject using a speaker without current authorization for the segment and purpose, silently substituting a voice or reordering segments, or claiming a generated artifact is committed when it is only a candidate.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized synthesis request pins the exact requested speaker or voice, model/checkpoint, profile, worker, and source version for the declared purpose.
citedParentCases.when: Media returns a generated-audio candidate or execution observation.
citedParentCases.then: Report requested and observed speaker/voice, model/checkpoint, profile, worker, and source identities separately for the exact output; preserve mismatch or unobserved identity as UNKNOWN and retain the output as synthetic media.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject silently substituting a speaker, voice, model, checkpoint, profile, or worker; inferring the effective identity from the request alone; or treating a configured identity as proof of the output's authorship, rights, or authenticity.

proposedFeatureSpecificP0Case.given: For an authorized source-speaker recording, current purpose-specific consent, and exact versioned weight/profile explicitly admitted for zero-shot use.

negativeCases: Missing/revoked/expired consent or unknown admission returns denied/UNKNOWN before inference.

cohortRows.currentCrosswalkReasoning: AUD-CLONE-006 is mapped to a coordinator-authored PDP-0 proposal for source-free synthetic voice design, without a human reference or speaker identity. The proposal defines the conditional pre-inference gate for applicable grants and exact model/checkpoint rights, requires rights/provenance on every future output, rejects Piper or synthetic placeholders as evidence of cloning or success, and leaves model adoption and priority pending owner disposition. Current speech and rights acceptance cases are conditional context; they do not themselves grant rights or admit inference. The feature is scoped to the proposed production-studio web consumer and its topology-bound physical/composite surfaces; owner approval, inference, implementation, runtime support, and qualification are not claimed.

citedParentCases.given: A requested transformation derives content from an identified source recording.
citedParentCases.when: the system evaluates whether the requested use is admitted.

citedParentCases.rejection: reject treating a similarity observation or source possession as a permitted-use decision.

citedParentCases.given: A requested synthetic or altered presenter involves an identifiable person, voice, or model.
citedParentCases.when: the product evaluates eligibility for the requested use.
citedParentCases.then: block use while applicable rights, consent, or license is missing, unknown, denied, restricted, revoked, or expired; disclosure remains separate from authorization.
citedParentCases.rejection: reject treating generated disclosure, an asserted right, or possession of a source as sufficient authorization.

citedParentCases.given: A creator requests singing-voice synthesis conditioned on an identifiable voice, source recording, or voice model.
citedParentCases.when: the product evaluates whether synthesis is permitted for the declared purpose.
citedParentCases.then: preserve voice, source, and model provenance and block use when applicable rights, consent, or license is missing, unknown, denied, restricted, revoked, or expired.
citedParentCases.rejection: reject inferring clearance from voice similarity, source possession, or the act of synthesis.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized reviewer declares a face or personally identifying information analysis purpose, exact source version, and the applicable owner policy.
citedParentCases.when: A face or PII observation is requested as evidence for a dependent use decision.
citedParentCases.then: Return only the declared detection or analysis observation with source version, time or region, and uncertainty, and keep its policy consequence tied to the named owner decision.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject inferring identity, consent, or use clearance from detection; missing or unknown purpose, authority, or policy leaves the dependent use blocked and unresolved.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized actor declares exact input versions, model or checkpoint, destination, purpose, and the applicable external-egress permission.
citedParentCases.when: A requested operation would transmit media or derived data outside the governed local scope.
citedParentCases.then: Identify the egress target and data class and require the applicable explicit permission before dispatch.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject implicit provider, model, or cloud fallback; missing, unknown, or denied egress permission blocks transmission.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized caller proposes use of each exact asset, voice, model or checkpoint, and font version and declares its purpose and scope.
citedParentCases.when: The product evaluates those components for project use or generation.
citedParentCases.then: Bind each component to its own rights-evidence reference, issuer or authority, scope, version, and decision state.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject inferring per-source permission from possession, package presence, a project-wide license, or similarity; absent, stale, revoked, incompatible, or unknown evidence blocks use.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized caller supplies captions, transcripts, prompts, or asset metadata from an external or user-supplied source marked as untrusted content.
citedParentCases.when: The product parses, summarizes, or passes that content to an agent or tool.
citedParentCases.then: Treat the content only as data; any proposed action remains attributed to an authorized actor and bound to the exact project revision.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject embedded content as authority to invoke privileged operations, change rights or egress, or mutate project state; an ambiguous instruction/data boundary blocks consequential action.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized editor requests a plugin, shader, or editor action with consequential access or effects and identifies the exact component version, permissions, and target state.
citedParentCases.when: The product evaluates that action for invocation.
citedParentCases.then: Require explicit, scoped, revocable authorization and disclose the requested permissions before invocation.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject inferring authority from installation, asset presence, or editor context; missing or unknown permission blocks invocation. Arbitrary user-authored shader execution remains unsupported by this product baseline.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized reviewer evaluates a voice request involving an identifiable person when required consent, impersonation, age-eligibility, or policy state is missing, unknown, disputed, or denied.

citedParentCases.then: Block the use and expose the unresolved policy reason for authorized review; the product defines no age threshold or legal eligibility test in this case.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject inferring consent or eligibility from similarity, public availability, source possession, or model capability.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized requester proposes a voice result that could target an identifiable person, but the applicable protected-person or consent-sensitive policy and review result are absent, unknown, disputed, or denied.

citedParentCases.then: Block or hold the request for an authorized owner-policy review without asserting a public-figure list or legal test.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject inferring eligibility from published recordings, requester assertion, public-figure status, or voice similarity.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized publisher declares viewer-analytics purpose, collected fields, retention and deletion scope, and a valid consent state for the exact viewer or session.

citedParentCases.then: Collect only consented, purpose-bounded fields, redact identity or secrets under the declared policy, and preserve consent and purpose provenance.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject collection or disclosure when consent is absent, revoked, unknown, or out of scope; viewing or interaction alone is not consent, and no retention duration is inferred.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized creator organizes a project containing immutable source-asset versions and requests library bins or nested collections.

citedParentCases.rejection: Reject replacing source assets, changing their versions, or applying ambiguous membership or hierarchy changes without confirmation.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized creator defines a smart bin using an explicit predicate over project assets and chooses live or snapshot membership.

citedParentCases.then: Return exact member-version references and label whether membership is live or a snapshot; distinguish observed attributes, inferred matches with uncertainty, unknown or unindexed attributes, and a known empty result.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject treating unknown or unindexed attributes as non-matches, silently changing snapshot membership, or implying that a smart bin mutates its source assets.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized editor submits a scene patch against an exact project and scene revision, and a later revision contains overlapping changes.
citedParentCases.when: The product evaluates whether the patch can be reconciled with the current revision.
citedParentCases.then: Return a local merge proposal bound to the base, left, and right revisions, identifying each overlapping conflict and preserving both source revisions; create a new revision only after explicit review and confirmation.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject silently applying a patch to a changed scene, choosing a conflict winner without authorization, or claiming a committed revision while the result is pending, unknown, or unavailable.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized project owner requests a portable backup of one exact project revision.
citedParentCases.when: The product prepares its backup manifest and restore proposal.
citedParentCases.then: Identify the exact project revision, included immutable asset versions, external references, and omitted, unavailable, or rights-restricted content; call the backup complete only when every required item and integrity check is accounted for, and restore as a new revision that preserves the originals.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject implying completeness when inclusion or integrity is unknown, silently replacing an external reference, or restoring over the source revision.

citedParentCases.given: An actor is authorized to search transcript content for an exact source-media or project version.
citedParentCases.when: The actor requests a semantic transcript search.
citedParentCases.then: Return bounded candidate matches anchored to the exact source version and transcript time range; distinguish unavailable transcript content, denied scope, unknown matching, and an empty candidate page.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject presenting candidates as complete when matching or continuation is unknown, or returning transcript content outside the admitted rights-and-retention scope.

citedParentCases.given: An actor is authorized to inspect possible duplicate or near-duplicate artifacts.
citedParentCases.when: the actor requests duplicate detection.
citedParentCases.then: Return bounded candidate groups that retain every source artifact identity and state the matching uncertainty.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject merging, replacing, or deleting any source artifact as a consequence of candidate detection.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized Studio creator searches the governed Media asset store for candidates for an explicitly declared intended-use scope.
citedParentCases.when: The product evaluates each immutable asset version for the requested license/use-scope filter.
citedParentCases.then: Return a candidate as eligible only when current authoritative per-version rights and license evidence explicitly permits the declared scope; preserve the exact asset version and evidence identity. Missing, unknown, denied, expired, revoked, restricted, or incompatible evidence never makes a candidate eligible, and unresolved evidence is reported as UNKNOWN or review-required rather than as an empty eligible result.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject inferring permission from searchable metadata, treating this filter as legal clearance, silently substituting a different asset or license, or claiming external-catalog search, ranking, or complete results.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized editor searches an admitted project for timeline, person, scene, or speaker facets with an explicit time range and exact project or source-version scope.
citedParentCases.when: The product evaluates the requested facet filters against indexed observations.
citedParentCases.then: Return bounded matches with exact immutable source-version references, matching time ranges, and observed or inferred provenance; report unknown or unindexed fields and partial matching separately from a known empty result.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject presenting an unindexed or uncertain facet as absent, claiming complete matches while continuation or indexing is unknown, or widening the search beyond authorized rights and retention scope.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized creator submits a visual or descriptive metadata query for assets within an explicit project and version scope.
citedParentCases.when: The product searches available visual observations and metadata.
citedParentCases.then: Return bounded candidate matches with exact source-version provenance, relevant time ranges where available, and match uncertainty; distinguish unavailable or unindexed evidence and unknown matching from a known empty result.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject representing similarity as a verified fact, dropping source-version provenance, claiming completeness when indexing or continuation is unknown, or exposing content outside admitted rights and retention scope.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized editor imports a sidecar or embedded caption track for an exact immutable media version and the format and rights are admitted.
citedParentCases.when: The product parses and validates the caption source and its timebase mapping.
citedParentCases.then: Return a reviewable caption-import result preserving source-file provenance, source version, language and format when known, caption timing, and any conversion or alignment uncertainty; do not alter the source media.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject silently shifting or dropping caption timing, claiming unknown language or alignment as verified, or registering or replacing a canonical artifact without the separately authorized action.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized editor requests a clip derived from an exact immutable source version with an explicit source-time range, output profile, purpose, and applicable rights.
citedParentCases.when: The product validates the range against the source timebase and prepares the derivation.
citedParentCases.then: Bind the candidate derivation to the exact source version and requested start and end times, disclose boundary quantization or uncertainty, and return job or candidate state without changing the source.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject substituting another source version, silently rounding or extending the requested range, implying a completed or registered artifact before that state is confirmed, or bypassing rights and profile admission.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized user searches the governed Media asset store by declared metadata and an intended-use rights scope.
citedParentCases.when: The product evaluates exact asset versions against available metadata and authoritative per-version rights evidence.
citedParentCases.then: Return bounded candidates with exact version and rights-evidence references; distinguish unknown or incomplete indexing from a known empty result. External catalogs are available only when a specific catalog and use are separately admitted.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject inferring permission from searchable metadata, calling search legal clearance, or claiming external-catalog, complete, or ranked results when those scopes are not admitted.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized editor supplies a source timecode with its exact source version, declared frame rate or timebase, and drop-frame or non-drop-frame mode.
citedParentCases.when: The product interprets or converts that timecode.
citedParentCases.then: Preserve the original label and mode and return an exact source-time mapping only when the declared rate, mode, and mapping are valid.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject ambiguous or invalid labels, mismatched rates, unknown mappings, silent drop-frame/non-drop-frame reinterpretation, or rounding across frame boundaries.

citedParentCases.when: the request is interpreted against a versioned project revision.
citedParentCases.then: produce a reviewable edit proposal before the consequential project state changes.
citedParentCases.rejection: reject silently committing an ambiguous or unreviewed proposal as an applied edit.

citedParentCases.given: A project has a confirmed revision and automatic checkpointing is in scope.
citedParentCases.when: the product checkpoints and later recovers project state after interruption.
citedParentCases.then: preserve the last confirmed revision and state which unsaved changes may be absent or lost before recovery is accepted.
citedParentCases.rejection: reject silently overwriting the confirmed revision or implying a durability or recovery-point guarantee not defined for the product.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized creator organizes a project containing immutable source-asset versions and requests library bins or nested collections.
citedParentCases.when: The creator proposes a hierarchy and assigns exact asset-version references to its bins.
citedParentCases.then: Return a reviewable, version-bound organization proposal that preserves each source identity and version and makes no project or asset mutation until explicitly confirmed.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject replacing source assets, changing their versions, or applying ambiguous membership or hierarchy changes without confirmation.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized creator defines a smart bin using an explicit predicate over project assets and chooses live or snapshot membership.
citedParentCases.when: Membership is evaluated against the declared project revision and predicate.
citedParentCases.then: Return exact member-version references and label whether membership is live or a snapshot; distinguish observed attributes, inferred matches with uncertainty, unknown or unindexed attributes, and a known empty result.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject treating unknown or unindexed attributes as non-matches, silently changing snapshot membership, or implying that a smart bin mutates its source assets.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized editor submits a scene patch against an exact project and scene revision, and a later revision contains overlapping changes.
citedParentCases.when: The product evaluates whether the patch can be reconciled with the current revision.
citedParentCases.then: Return a local merge proposal bound to the base, left, and right revisions, identifying each overlapping conflict and preserving both source revisions; create a new revision only after explicit review and confirmation.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject silently applying a patch to a changed scene, choosing a conflict winner without authorization, or claiming a committed revision while the result is pending, unknown, or unavailable.

citedParentCases.given: An authorized project owner requests a portable backup of one exact project revision.
citedParentCases.when: The product prepares its backup manifest and restore proposal.
citedParentCases.then: Identify the exact project revision, included immutable asset versions, external references, and omitted, unavailable, or rights-restricted content; call the backup complete only when every required item and integrity check is accounted for, and restore as a new revision that preserves the originals.
citedParentCases.rejection: Reject implying completeness when inclusion or integrity is unknown, silently replacing an external reference, or restoring over the source revision.
